summary: Initial answer latency increased for chat completions after model variant + runtime config change
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports a ~3x increase in time-to-first-token (TTFB) for chat completions after we rolled out runtime 1.5.0 and a model variant swap for redwood-instruct-2.7.

Impact: Multiple production teams at Harmonia Health observe initial token latency rising from ~120ms to 350-450ms for short prompts (<=64 tokens). This impacts UI perceived responsiveness for chat features and has triggered degraded user experience.

Observed start: After a coordinated push on 2026-03-09 (runtime 1.5.0 + model variant routing tweak) — spike aligns with deploy timestamps.

Temporary status: Customers routed to fallback variant sometimes see normal latency; however, most requests to primary routing path hit the elevated TTFB consistently.

Additional notes: No 5xx spike was observed; throughput and downstream token emission remain normal. Symptoms are specifically elevated latency before the first token is emitted (TTFB).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a chat completion request using the redwood-instruct-2.7 model in prod-us-west
2) Use short prompts (~10-50 tokens) and request streaming responses with default timeout
3) Observe initial token arrival time in client telemetry (compare to baseline collected prior to 2026-03-09).
4) Repeat routing request header to prefer primary variant vs fallback variant to compare times.

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: kernel selection/quantization path in 1.5.0 may introduce an extra compilation or memory migration causing first-token stalls.
Checked autoscaler logs: no cold-start spikes on nodes; GPU utilization steady. Not a capacity shortage.
Compared routing traces: requests routed to fallback variant (older model binary) do not show the delay -> points to variant-specific runtime behavior.
Heap and GPU memory snapshots show more frequent allocation churn during initialization for primary variant under runtime 1.5.0.
Investigated recent PRs: runtime PR #981 modified kernel cache eviction heuristics; model-registry PR #412 changed variant tag ordering for routing (can alter kernel choice). Both merged 2026-03-09.
Reproduced locally in staging by forcing runtime 1.5.0 + primary variant: captured a 300-500ms stall in serve startup for first request in a session when KV cache warm but kernel rebind occurs.
customer_communication: 2026-03-10T09:12Z - Maya Chen: Acknowledged customer's report, requested request IDs and sample prompt. SLA first response within 2 hours.
2026-03-10T11:44Z - Customer (Harmonia Health): Provided three example request_ids and client-side timings. Confirmed issue started after midnight on 2026-03-09.
2026-03-10T14:05Z - Maya Chen: Shared workaround to pin to fallback variant via 'variant_preference=fallback' header and asked customer to confirm improvement.
2026-03-10T14:22Z - Customer: Confirmed TTFB dropped back to expected ~130ms when pinned to fallback variant.
mitigation_steps: 1) Short-term customer workaround: add header variant_preference=fallback to route away from affected primary variant.
2) Ops: rollback runtime 1.5.0 on the affected us-west pool if multiple enterprise customers confirm impact (pending Prod runbook approval).
3) Engineering: revert runtime PR #981 kernel cache eviction change on a canary pool and measure TTFB impact.
resolution_notes: Action taken: Eng team prepared a canary revert of the kernel eviction heuristic (PR rollback) and deployed to a small subset of primary pools in us-west on 2026-03-11.
Result: Canary pools showed TTFB p50 reduced from ~370ms to ~130ms for redwood-instruct-2.7, aligning with fallback behavior. No other regressions observed in throughput.
Customer communication: On 2026-03-11 18:00Z, we coordinated with Harmonia Health to route their production traffic to the reverted pool; customer confirmed improved UX.

Permanent follow-up: Engineering will land a focused fix to kernel selection logic that avoids rebinds at first request and update runtime 1.5.1. A post-deploy validation will include a synthetic TTFB smoke test for pinned short prompts.
postmortem_actions: Root cause: unsafe kernel cache eviction in runtime 1.5.0 combined with new model-variant ordering caused kernel rebinds on first token for certain model binaries, producing a 300-500ms initial stall.
Action item 1: Add TTFB synthetic check to pre-deploy canary health tests for all runtime upgrades (owner: SRE, due 2026-03-19).
Action item 2: Engineering to implement lazy rebind and preserve warmed kernel handles for variant swaps (owner: Serving Runtime, PR tracked).
Action item 3: Update rollout runbook to include explicit verification of short-prompt p50 TTFB across affected regions before fully promoting runtime.
